ai.cloud_llm.label: ship a cloud LLM / AI client or endpoint that can receive user content
ai.cloud_llm.ctx: TRK-05: free-text prompts, and often photos or screen context, sent to a third-party model. Share of the apps with per-app detail in this dashboard.

ai.kids_trackers.label: of kids-category apps embed ad / attribution trackers
ai.kids_trackers.ctx: TGAP-03: COPPA and the App Store Kids Category prohibit third-party advertising to children. {kidsApps} kids-genre apps in this batch.

ai.proximity.label: reference nearby-device APIs (BLE / UWB / Wi-Fi / Bonjour)
ai.proximity.ctx: DCS-07: proximity signals can fingerprint the user's physical and household environment. A reference shows the capability, not a scan of the user's surroundings. Share of the apps with per-app detail in this dashboard.

footprint.average_size.label: is the average app download size in this batch

footprint.avg_permissions.label: permission purpose strings declared by the average app
footprint.avg_permissions.ctx: Every NS*UsageDescription in Info.plist, sensitive or not. A declaration is a statement of intent, not proof the API is called.

footprint.heavily_tracked.label: of apps are heavily tracked (10+ distinct tracker SDKs)
footprint.heavily_tracked.ctx: {apps}. Median across the whole batch, apps with no trackers included, is {median}.

footprint.largest_app.label: is the largest app ({app})
footprint.largest_app.ctx: Bigger binaries mean more third-party SDKs and attack surface.

footprint.size_confound.label: is how strongly app size alone predicts the finding count
footprint.size_confound.ctx: Across {apps} apps. Bigger binaries carry more third-party code, so part of a large finding count is volume rather than behaviour. Read a per-app tally against its size, not on its own.

footprint.top_endpoint_owner.label: of apps reference {owner}-owned endpoints
footprint.top_endpoint_owner.ctx: Most common endpoint owner by resolved network destination.

security.ats_arbitrary.label: weaken App Transport Security with arbitrary network loads
security.ats_arbitrary.ctx: {oneIn} apps opt out of HTTPS-only networking.

security.encryption_coverage.label: of analysed binaries are FairPlay-encrypted at rest
security.encryption_coverage.ctx: Across {binaries} Mach-O binaries. Encrypted code hides its strings, so tracker and secret counts on this page are a floor, not a census.{blindNote}

security.high_or_critical.label: carry at least one high- or critical-severity finding
security.high_or_critical.ctx: {critical} critical and {high} high findings across the batch; the headline counts apps.

security.insecure_storage.label: show a weak data-at-rest setting (file protection off, keychain readable while locked)
security.insecure_storage.ctx: Counts findings at low severity or above. The info-level references are left out, and so is the backup-exclusion API: that is a mitigation (MASWE-0006), not a weakness.

security.no_arc.label: of analysed binaries are built without ARC memory management
security.no_arc.ctx: Across {binaries} Mach-O binaries where the flag is readable. Manual retain/release is where use-after-free bugs live.

security.no_canary.label: of analysed binaries ship without stack canaries
security.no_canary.ctx: Across {binaries} Mach-O binaries where the flag is readable. Canaries are the cheapest defence against stack smashing.

security.secrets.label: ship a hard-coded credential in the binary or resources
security.secrets.ctx: API keys, tokens or credentials matched by format or entropy. Public client identifiers (a Firebase API key in its configuration file) are identifiers by design and are not counted.

security.weak_crypto.label: reference weak hash or non-cryptographic random APIs (MD5 / SHA-1, rand())
security.weak_crypto.ctx: An import shows the API is available to the app's code, not that it protects anything with it; MASWE-0008 and MASWE-0012 turn on how it is used. Common for checksums and cache keys.

security.webview_bridge.label: configure a WebView in a way MASWE flags
security.webview_bridge.ctx: Legacy UIWebView, file-URL access, remote inspection in release, or a JS bridge injected into every frame. Plain WKWebView use and ordinary message handlers are inventory and are not counted.

sovereignty.foreign_owner.label: embed a tracker whose owner is based outside {home}
sovereignty.foreign_owner.ctx: Relative to the storefront this batch was drawn from. Cross-border transfers are what GDPR Chapter V and data-residency laws regulate; whether one happens is decided at runtime.

sovereignty.top_endpoint_country.label: of apps reference endpoints owned by a company based in {country}
sovereignty.top_endpoint_country.ctx: The owning organisation's home jurisdiction, from the tracker database. Not where a server is hosted: that needs DNS and GeoIP, which a static scan does not do.

sovereignty.top_tracker_country.label: embed a tracker from a company based in {country}
sovereignty.top_tracker_country.ctx: Data-sovereignty signal: the tracker owner's home jurisdiction. Embedding shows the SDK or its endpoint is present, not a transfer. Share of the apps with per-app detail in this dashboard.

surv.att_prompt.label: ask for App Tracking Transparency consent to track you across apps
surv.att_prompt.ctx: An ATT prompt means the app wants the IDFA for cross-app/-site tracking.

surv.background_exfil.label: can run network work in the background above info
surv.background_exfil.ctx: Background modes and silent pushes are how an app does work while not in the foreground. Declaring one is normal; this counts only the ones rated above info.

surv.biometrics.label: read motion sensors or raw touch data (behavioural-biometric inputs)
surv.biometrics.ctx: Accelerometer, gyroscope and touch coordinate/force capture. Face ID is not counted: it is local authentication and has its own card. Counts findings at low severity or above; the info-level references nearly every app carries are left out.

surv.contacts_permission.label: request access to your contacts / address book
surv.contacts_permission.ctx: Contact graphs are a common social-graph data source. Share of the apps with per-app detail in this dashboard.

surv.content_access.label: reference clipboard, contacts, photo-library or calendar APIs
surv.content_access.ctx: Pasteboard reads and address-book or photo access are common over-collection signals. Counts findings that meet two WP 248 criteria; API references alone are info and left out.

surv.data_broker.label: embed a known third-party data broker
surv.data_broker.ctx: X-Mode / Outlogic / SafeGraph / Cuebiq-class location & behaviour brokers. Share of the apps with per-app detail in this dashboard.

surv.face_id.label: use Face ID / biometric authentication
surv.face_id.ctx: Local biometric auth (LocalAuthentication) is a privacy-preserving signal. Share of the apps with per-app detail in this dashboard.

surv.fingerprinting.label: reference device-identifier or fingerprinting APIs (IDFA / IDFV, hardware probes)
surv.fingerprinting.ctx: A reference shows the capability is in the app, not that it builds a fingerprint. Counts findings that meet two WP 248 criteria; API references alone are info and left out.

surv.location.label: may track location in the background
surv.location.ctx: Always authorization declared in Info.plist, or visit, region or significant-change monitoring with that key present: systematic monitoring of location data, WP 248 criteria 3 and 4. Location used only while the app is open is info and not counted here.

surv.location_permission.label: request access to your location
surv.location_permission.ctx: Across when-in-use, always and temporary precision variants. Share of the apps with per-app detail in this dashboard.

surv.microphone_permission.label: request microphone access
surv.microphone_permission.ctx: Audio capture permission declared in Info.plist. Share of the apps with per-app detail in this dashboard.

surv.session_replay.label: run a session-replay SDK that can record taps, scrolls and screens
surv.session_replay.ctx: FullStory, Quantum Metric, LogRocket, Smartlook, or a vendor's session-replay module (Amplitude, Mixpanel, Dynatrace), found by framework name or tracker domain. Linked is not recording: the SDK may be off or masking the screen. Share of the apps with per-app detail in this dashboard.

surv.top_permission.label: of apps request access to {what}
surv.top_permission.ctx: {key}: the most-declared sensitive permission in this batch, in {apps} apps.

tracking.advertising.label: embed at least one advertising / ad-mediation SDK
tracking.advertising.ctx: Ad SDKs are the most common vector for cross-app identifiers and RTB data sharing. Share of the apps with per-app detail in this dashboard.

tracking.analytics.label: ship an analytics SDK that profiles in-app behaviour
tracking.analytics.ctx: Firebase / Amplitude / Mixpanel-class event and funnel tracking. Share of the apps with per-app detail in this dashboard.

tracking.any_tracker.label: of apps embed at least one third-party tracker SDK
tracking.any_tracker.ctx: {instances} tracker instances across {distinct} distinct SDKs in this batch.

tracking.most_prevalent.label: of apps contain the most prevalent tracker ({name})

tracking.outlier.label: tracker SDKs in a single app ({app})
tracking.outlier.ctx: Median among apps that carry at least one tracker is {median}. One app at this scale skews every per-app average on this page.

tracking.owners_per_app.label: distinct tracker companies embedded in the average app
tracking.owners_per_app.ctx: {owners} different tracker owners seen across the batch.

tracking.per_app.label: trackers in the average tracked app
tracking.per_app.ctx: Counting only apps that ship at least one tracker. Worst: {worst}.

footprint.apple_policy_gap.label: of apps carry at least one Apple App Store policy gap
footprint.apple_policy_gap.ctx: Required-Reason API declarations, tracking-domain declarations, ATT consent or the kids category. {cleanNote}

footprint.most_findings.label: critical and high findings in the app carrying the most ({app})
footprint.most_findings.ctx: {cleanest} Apps are ordered by this tally.

footprint.busiest_category.label: findings for the average app in the busiest category ({name})
footprint.busiest_category.ctx: Mean across the {count} apps in that category · batch median {median} findings per app.

footprint.top_cluster.label: of apps raise a finding in {cluster}
footprint.top_cluster.ctx: The most frequently hit cluster: an OWASP MASVS control group, or Apple App Store policy.

footprint.top_maswe.label: findings in the most-hit OWASP MASWE weakness class
footprint.top_maswe.ctx: {weakness} ({id}). Counted as findings across {apps} apps, not as a share of them: one app can raise this weakness many times.
